title: Marginal usage-triggered hiring corridor (May 2026)
content:
Summary:
This spreadsheet-style note defines a headcount corridor and hiring runbook that is driven by marginal usage growth (tokens/month). Purpose: reduce lag between demand signal and hiring while protecting runway when price compression occurs. This is intentionally lightweight and trade-off focused — intended for review with FP&A and SRE leads.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline month (May 2026) tokens served: 120M tokens/month (mixed gen + embeddings).
- Baseline blended price: $0.0038 per 1k tokens (weighted across routes).
- Baseline contribution margin per token after infra: $0.0017/1k tokens.
- Average fully-loaded engineer cost (incl. benefits): $220k/year (~$18.3k/month).
- Average infra variable cost per 100M tokens: $45k/month (GPU + egress + spot variance).
- Time-to-hire (avg for infra/serving roles): 9 weeks.

Top-level scenario table (illustrative):
Scenario | Tokens/mo (M) | Price per 1k $ | Monthly revenue $ | Variable infra $ | Gross margin $ | Hiring trigger (tokens delta/mo)
Base    | 120           | 0.0038         | 456.0k            | 45.0k            | 411.0k          | n/a
Growth  | 180 (+60)     | 0.0034         | 67.5k            | 532.6k          | hire 2 infra engs if > +50M sustained 6w
Surge   | 260 (+140)    | 0.0029         | 754.0k            | 97.0k            | 657.0k          | hire 4 infra + 1 SRE if > +120M sustained 8w
Compression | 95 (-25)   | 0.0032         | 304.0k            | 35.6k            | 268.4k          | freeze hires; pull from reserve pool

Notes on table calculations:
- Monthly revenue = (Tokens/mo * Price per 1k). Prices shown are scenario-adjusted to reflect tiered discounting and market pressure.
- Variable infra estimated by GPU-hours required for gen traffic + egress. These scale superlinearly after 200M tokens due to longer seq lengths in the surge scenario.
- Gross margin = revenue - variable infra (does not include hiring or fixed opex).

Headcount corridor (role-level)
Role | Baseline FTE | Growth threshold (tokens delta/mo) | Add FTE when threshold hit | Max corridor FTE
Infra Eng | 9 | +50M | +2 per +50M | 15
SRE       | 4 | +100M | +1 per +100M | 7
Billing/RevOps | 3 | +80M revenue equivalent | +1 per +80M rev | 5
Solutions SE | 6 | +60M (product-led accounts) | +1 per +60M tokens localized | 9
Data Ops / Observability | 2 | +120M | +1 | 4

Hiring mechanics & timing
- Signal: rolling 6-week token delta measured by product-route and region. Use 3-week and 6-week rolling averages to avoid one-off surges.
- Pre-approve bench: maintain a 6-week contractor bench (budgeted as 0.8 FTE equiv) to temporarily cover infra work while hires ramp.
- Trigger cadence: if 6-week rolling delta > threshold AND 3-week > 60% of that delta, create a hiring request.
- Acceleration clause: If delta expected to persist (sales pipeline or deal-specific data), allow immediate contractor-to-perm conversion budget up to 3 months of salary.

Pricing sensitivity breakouts (marginal analysis):
- Elasticity model (simplified): assume token demand elasticity e = -0.25 for quoted price moves in our bands. A price drop of 10% => +2.5% tokens. Conversely, a price increase compresses tokens.
- Quick check: moving from $0.0038 to $0.0034 (-10.5%) gives +2.6% demand, not enough alone to justify hiring. But customers react nonlinearly by segment: platform accounts (top 5) drive 40% of marginal tokens, their elasticity is higher (e~-0.6).
- Worst-case profit sensitivity table (monthly):
Price | Tokens/mo | Revenue | Infra cost | Hiring budget (new FTEs) | Net margin delta vs base
$0.0042 | 114 | 479k | 43k | 0 | +8.5%
$0.0038 | 120 | 456k | 45k | 0 | base
$0.0034 | 180 | 612k | 67.5k | +$36.6k (2 hires) | +6.2%
$0.0029 | 260 | 754k | 97k | +$183.6k (5 hires) | +21.0%
$0.0024 | 380 | 912k | 165k | +$394k (10 hires) | +25.5% (but runway risk if price compression persistent)

Interpretation: higher volumes at lower price can still increase nominal margin in many cases due to fixed-cost leverage, but hiring cadence must be conservative because mis-timed hiring increases fixed burn and amplifies downside. The corridor is therefore asymmetric: faster ramp-up for infra contractors, slower perm hiring.

Runbook (decision tree summary)
1) Signal detected: Compute 3w/6w rolling deltas by route and region. Tag deltas by customer cohort (enterprise, mid-market, platform).
2) Check revenue per token by cohort — if > 2x baseline, prioritize immediate SRE/infra bench.
3) If growth triggers hiring: open req (finance+hr pre-check), post to contractor bench, and prep 9-week perm hire timeline.
4) If price compression + token decline: pause non-critical hiring, move hiring budget to retention/upsell for top accounts, retrofit burst reserve for 90 days.
5) Quarterly review: reconcile forecast vs actual, update price elasticity coefficients for top 20 accounts.

Open questions & risks:
- How to attribute tokens to 'account' vs 'platform' when multi-tenant routes exist? (engineering input needed; see JIRA: ENG-7648).
- Our elasticity estimates are rough and derived from 6 months of promotional price tests. Need an A/B test plan to validate elasticity by cohort (Confluence: pricing-ab-test-scope).
- Time-to-hire variance by geography not modeled (US vs EU hiring can be +3 weeks).
- Contract bench cost initially budgeted at 0.8 FTE at 1.25x equivalent hourly rates; risk that contractor premium reduces margin advantage on short-term hires.

Immediate asks for review meeting (May 18 2026):
- FP&A: sanity-check the average fully-loaded cost numbers and contractor multipliers.
- Eng leadership: confirm 6-week rolling signal feasibility and instrumentation ownership.
- GTM: highlight any large deals in pipeline that would materially change near-term tokens.

Appendix — quick sensitivity formulas (for spreadsheet):
- monthly_revenue = tokens_m * price_per_1k * (1/1000)
- infra_cost = base_infra + scale_coef * max(0, tokens_m - inflection_point) / 1e6 * infra_unit_cost
- hire_count = floor(max(0, tokens_delta - threshold) / per_hire_token_capacity)

Versions & notes:
- v0.1 (2026-05-02) initial draft
- v0.2 (2026-05-14) add surge scenario and hiring cadence clarifications

Editors: Aisha Patel (finance lead), Diego Marquez (FP&A), Lena Cho (SRE), Marcus Reed (Head of FP&A)
